title: Story 06: Parallel Independent Tasks
pmResponse:
# Project Manager Action Plan: Story 06 — Parallel Independent Tasks

> **Note on testing mode:** Per my operating constraints, I am not executing any commands or reading files. Below is the complete, ordered action plan with every `agt` command I would run, the reasoning behind each, the resulting issue hierarchy, blockages, and comments.

---

## 1. Situation Analysis & Reasoning

**Two incoming requests:**

| # | Request | Type | Codebase | Team |
|---|---------|------|----------|------|
| 1 | "Add pagination to the issue list CLI command" | **Feature** | Library (agentrack CLI) | Library sub-team |
| 2 | "Fix the dark mode toggle on the webapp" | **Bug** | Webapp | Webapp sub-team |

**Key assessment:**
- ✅ **Different codebases** — the CLI lives in the library; dark mode lives in the webapp. No file-level conflicts.
- ✅ **No logical dependency** — paginating `agt list` has nothing to do with the webapp's dark mode toggle. Neither blocks the other.
- ✅ **Different sub-teams** — the Library agents and Webapp agents can work simultaneously without contention.

**Decision:** Create **two independent parent issues**, each with its own full phase-lifecycle broken into child issues. Create sequential blockages **within** each track (phases must happen in order), but **zero blockages between** the two tracks so they run in parallel.

**Phase flows applied:**
- Feature (CLI pagination): `Plan → Dev → Validate → Release`
- Bug (dark mode): `Reproduce → Dev → Validate → Release`

**Resource note / gap I detected:** The Webapp sub-team has **no dedicated releaser** (unlike the Library sub-team which has `library-releaser`). I will temporarily assign the webapp release step to `webapp-developer` and file an `idea` issue flagging this gap for the project-manager to triage.

---

## 2. Target Issue Hierarchy

```
#1  Add pagination to the issue list CLI command          [feature, epic]  todo   (priority 3)
 ├─ #2  Design pagination for the issue list CLI command   [feature, task] todo → library-architect   (Plan)
 ├─ #3  Implement pagination in the issue list CLI command [feature, task] todo → library-developer  (Dev)      ⛔ blocked by #2
 ├─ #4  Validate pagination in the issue list CLI command  [feature, task] todo → library-validator  (Validate) ⛔ blocked by #3
 └─ #5  Release pagination for the issue list CLI command  [feature, chore] todo → library-releaser  (Release)  ⛔ blocked by #4

#6  Fix the dark mode toggle on the webapp               [bug, epic]      todo   (priority 2)
 ├─ #7  Reproduce the dark mode toggle bug                 [bug, task]     todo → webapp-validator   (Reproduce)
 ├─ #8  Fix the dark mode toggle bug                       [bug, task]     todo → webapp-developer  (Dev)      ⛔ blocked by #7
 ├─ #9  Validate the dark mode toggle fix                  [bug, task]     todo → webapp-validator   (Validate) ⛔ blocked by #8
 └─ #10 Release the dark mode toggle fix                   [bug, chore]    todo → webapp-developer* (Release)  ⛔ blocked by #9
                                                                       (*fallback — no webapp-releaser exists)

#11 Consider adding a dedicated webapp-releaser agent      [idea, chore]   idea → project-manager  (gap flagged)
```

**Critical point on parallelism:** There is **no** blockage connecting {#1–#5} to {#6–#10}. The two tracks are fully independent and can proceed concurrently from the very start. The immediately-actionable issues on day one are **#2** (Plan, library) and **#7** (Reproduce, webapp) — both unblocked.

---

## 3. Complete Command Sequence (in execution order)

### Phase A — Create the CLI Pagination feature track (Library)

**A1.** Create the parent epic.
```bash
agt create "Add pagination to the issue list CLI command" \
  --description "Add pagination support to the `agt list` CLI command so users can page through large issue lists. Full feature track: Plan → Dev → Validate → Release. Independent of (parallel to) the webapp dark mode fix." \
  --tags feature,epic \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3
```
*Reasoning:* Top-level container for the feature. `epic` + `feature` tags. Priority 3 = normal feature. Status `todo` until all children complete. → **returns ID, assume `1`**.

**A2.** Plan phase → `library-architect`.
```bash
agt create "Design pagination for the issue list CLI command" \
  --description "Plan/architecture phase: Design pagination for `agt list`. Define CLI flags (e.g. --page, --limit/--per-page), default page size, offset-vs-cursor strategy, output formatting, and total-count display. Produce a spec the developer can implement against." \
  --tags feature,task \
  --assignee library-architect \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 1 \
  --priority 3
```
*Reasoning:* First phase in the feature flow. `library-architect` owns the planning phase. This is the **only unblocked child** initially — work can begin immediately. → **assume `2`**.

**A3.** Dev phase → `library-developer`.
```bash
agt create "Implement pagination in the issue list CLI command" \
  --description "Development phase: Implement the pagination feature in `agt list` following the architect's spec (issue #2)." \
  --tags feature,task \
  --assignee library-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 1 \
  --priority 3
```
*Reasoning:* Dev phase, assigned to `library-developer`. Created now but will be blocked until the spec (#2) is done. → **assume `3`**.

**A4.** Validate phase → `library-validator`.
```bash
agt create "Validate pagination in the issue list CLI command" \
  --description "Validation phase: Write unit/integration tests for the pagination feature and verify behavior against the spec. Cover edge cases: empty result sets, last page, out-of-range page numbers, large page sizes, default behavior with no flags." \
  --tags feature,task \
  --assignee library-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 1 \
  --priority 3
```
*Reasoning:* Validate phase, assigned to `library-validator`. Blocked until implementation (#3) lands. → **assume `4`**.

**A5.** Release phase → `library-releaser`.
```bash
agt create "Release pagination for the issue list CLI command" \
  --description "Release phase: Run the full test suite, update/generate docs for the new pagination flags, build the package, and publish the updated `agt list` to npm. Bump version per semver." \
  --tags feature,chore \
  --assignee library-releaser \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 1 \
  --priority 3
```
*Reasoning:* Release phase, assigned to `library-releaser`. Final gate; blocked until validation (#4) passes. → **assume `5`**.

**A6.** Wire up the sequential blockages within this track.
```bash
agt blockages add 3 --by 2     # Dev (#3) blocked until Plan (#2) is done
agt blockages add 4 --by 3     # Validate (#4) blocked until Dev (#3) is done
agt blockages add 5 --by 4     # Release (#5) blocked until Validate (#4) is done
```
*Reasoning:* Enforces the canonical feature phase order. Note: I deliberately do **not** add any blockage referencing the dark-mode track.

---

### Phase B — Create the Dark Mode bug track (Webapp)

**B1.** Create the parent epic.
```bash
agt create "Fix the dark mode toggle on the webapp" \
  --description "The dark mode toggle on the webapp is not functioning correctly. Full bug track: Reproduce → Dev → Validate → Release. Independent of (parallel to) the CLI pagination feature." \
  --tags bug,epic \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2
```
*Reasoning:* Top-level container. `bug` + `epic` tags. Priority 2 — a UX-facing bug, slightly above a normal feature. → **assume `6`**.

**B2.** Reproduce phase → `webapp-validator`.
```bash
agt create "Reproduce the dark mode toggle bug" \
  --description "Reproduce the dark mode toggle bug. Document exact reproduction steps, expected vs actual behavior, affected browsers/environments, and attach screenshots. This report feeds the developer's fix." \
  --tags bug,task \
  --assignee webapp-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 6 \
  --priority 2
```
*Reasoning:* Bugs start with reproduction. `webapp-validator` owns bug reproduction + validation. This is the **unblocked starting point** of the webapp track — can begin immediately, in parallel with #2. → **assume `7`**.

**B3.** Dev (Fix) phase → `webapp-developer`.
```bash
agt create "Fix the dark mode toggle bug" \
  --description "Development phase: Diagnose and fix the root cause of the dark mode toggle malfunction, using the reproduction report (issue #7)." \
  --tags bug,task \
  --assignee webapp-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 6 \
  --priority 2
```
*Reasoning:* Dev/fix phase, assigned to `webapp-developer`. Blocked until the bug is reproduced (#7). → **assume `8`**.

**B4.** Validate phase → `webapp-validator`.
```bash
agt create "Validate the dark mode toggle fix" \
  --description "Validation phase: Confirm the fix resolves the reported bug. Run E2E tests, verify both light and dark modes toggle and persist correctly, check across major browsers, and confirm no regressions." \
  --tags bug,task \
  --assignee webapp-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 6 \
  --priority 2
```
*Reasoning:* Validation returns to `webapp-validator`. Blocked until the fix (#8) is in. → **assume `9`**.

**B5.** Release phase → `webapp-developer` *(fallback — see note)*.
```bash
agt create "Release the dark mode toggle fix" \
  --description "Release phase: Build the webapp and deploy the dark mode toggle fix. NOTE: assigned to webapp-developer as a fallback because the webapp sub-team has no dedicated releaser role (see issue #11)." \
  --tags bug,chore \
  --assignee webapp-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 6 \
  --priority 2
```
*Reasoning:* Final gate. The Webapp team has no `webapp-releaser`, so I assign to `webapp-developer` (who can handle build/deploy) and flag the structural gap separately (#11). → **assume `10`**.

**B6.** Wire up the sequential blockages within this track.
```bash
agt blockages add 8 --by 7     # Dev/Fix (#8) blocked until Reproduce (#7) is done
agt blockages add 9 --by 8     # Validate (#9) blocked until Fix (#8) is done
agt blockages add 10 --by 9    # Release (#10) blocked until Validate (#9) is done
```
*Reasoning:* Enforces the canonical bug phase order. Again, **no cross-track blockages** — this is what makes the two tracks parallel.

---

### Phase C — Stakeholder comments on each parent

**C1.** Document the plan on the CLI pagination epic.
```bash
agt comments add 1 --content "Kicked off the pagination feature as a 4-phase track (Plan → Dev → Validate → Release), entirely within the Library codebase. First actionable item is the architecture spec (#2) assigned to @library-architect — unblocked now. This track is fully independent of the webapp dark mode fix (#6) and runs in parallel; no cross-dependencies exist."
```
*Reasoning:* Keeps stakeholders informed of scope, sequencing, and the parallelism decision. Good PM communication hygiene.

**C2.** Document the plan on the dark mode epic.
```bash
agt comments add 6 --content "Kicked off the dark mode toggle fix as a 4-phase bug track (Reproduce → Dev → Validate → Release), entirely within the Webapp codebase. First actionable item is the reproduction report (#7) assigned to @webapp-validator — unblocked now. This track is fully independent of the CLI pagination feature (#1) and runs in parallel. Heads-up: the webapp team has no dedicated releaser, so the release step (#10) is temporarily assigned to @webapp-developer. I've opened issue #11 to address this role gap."
```
*Reasoning:* Transparent about the plan, the parallel execution, and — importantly — the resource gap so it's not a silent risk.

---

### Phase D — Flag the detected resource gap

**D1.** File an `idea` issue for the missing webapp-releaser.
```bash
agt create "Consider adding a dedicated webapp-releaser agent" \
  --description "The Webapp sub-team (webapp-developer, webapp-styler, webapp-validator) has no dedicated release-phase agent, unlike the Library sub-team which has library-releaser. Webapp release/deploy work currently falls back to webapp-developer, which pulls a developer off implementation work and creates a minor bottleneck on the critical path. Consider adding a webapp-releaser role (build, deploy, smoke-test) to mirror library-releaser and keep role separation clean." \
  --tags idea,chore \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status idea
```
*Reasoning:* This is work outside the scope of both current requests but directly surfaced by planning them. Per my operating protocol, I file out-of-scope findings as `idea` issues assigned to `project-manager` for triage rather than silently absorbing them. → **assume `11`**.

---

### Phase E — Verification (confirm the structure landed correctly)

**E1.** Confirm each track's children.
```bash
agt list --parentId 1     # Expect #2, #3, #4, #5
agt list --parentId 6     # Expect #7, #8, #9, #10
```
*Reasoning:* Sanity-check the parent/child linkage before handing off.

**E2.** Confirm the blockage graph is correct (and implicitly confirm no cross-track links exist).
```bash
agt blockages list 3      # Expect: blocked by #2 only
agt blockages list 4      # Expect: blocked by #3 only
agt blockages list 5      # Expect: blocked by #4 only
agt blockages list 8      # Expect: blocked by #7 only
agt blockages list 9      # Expect: blocked by #8 only
agt blockages list 10     # Expect: blocked by #9 only
```
*Reasoning:* Verifies the sequential-within-track, parallel-between-tracks structure. Critically, no issue in {#1–#5} should appear as a blocker of any issue in {#6–#10} and vice versa.

**E3.** Confirm the two day-one issues are genuinely unblocked.
```bash
agt blockages list 2      # Expect: no blockages (Plan is ready to start)
agt blockages list 7      # Expect: no blockages (Reproduce is ready to start)
```
*Reasoning:* These are the two issues I expect agents to pick up immediately, in parallel. Confirming they have zero blockers validates the parallel-kickoff plan.

---

## 4. What Happens Next (Execution Hand-off)

At the moment the plan is in place, the state is:

- **#2 (Plan, library-architect)** and **#7 (Reproduce, webapp-validator)** are both **unblocked** → both sub-teams start working **immediately and concurrently**.
- As each phase completes, the responsible agent adds a results comment, sets their issue to `done`, and the next phase's blockage is resolved (via `agt blockages resolve <child> --by <completed>`) so the downstream agent can begin.
- The two tracks never wait on each other.
- When all children of a parent are `done`, I (PM) close out the parent epic.
- **#11** (releaser gap) sits in `idea` for the project-manager to triage at their discretion — it does not block either track.

---

## 5. Summary

- **Did I complete the task?** Yes — produced a complete, executable plan that creates two independent, fully-phased issue tracks.
- **Anything interesting found?** I detected that the **Webapp sub-team has no dedicated releaser** (the Library sub-team does). I worked around it by assigning the release step to `webapp-developer` and filed **#11** as an `idea` for the project-manager, rather than leaving it as a silent risk.
- **Unexpected problems solved:** None blocking. The only judgment call was the releaser gap, handled proactively.
- **Open questions / future items:**
  - **#11** — Should we add a `webapp-releaser` role? Awaiting project-manager triage.
  - If the dark mode fix turns out to require CSS/visual rework, `webapp-styler` could be engaged as a sub-step of the Dev phase (#8) — I'd spin that off as a child of #8 only if the reproduction report confirms a styling root cause. Not pre-created to avoid speculative overhead.
feedback: Agent correctly recognized the two items as unrelated (no Initiative grandparent), enforced sequential within-track dependencies with zero cross-track blockages, avoided a styler for the bug, and started the bug with reproduction by webapp-validator. However, multiple critical errors: (1) used library-architect for pagination planning instead of library-developer — expected explicitly notes pagination is simple enough for the developer; (2) created a release phase for the webapp bug and assigned it to webapp-developer, when expected says no separate release exists (webapp deploys automatically); (3) never created the per-track sync/verify tracker tasks (tag task,sync, assigned to project-manager, blocked by last worker child) — a complete miss on the sync pattern; (4) left parents in todo instead of transitioning them to in-progress; (5) added incorrect tags (epic on parents, parent-type tags on children instead of just task); (6) filed an out-of-scope idea issue and flagged a non-existent releaser gap based on the wrong premise that webapp needs a release. The core parallelism insight is sound, but execution diverges substantially from the expected lifecycle.
